summary: SpaceStories: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational web application that explores the stories behind equipment left on the Moon and Mars after space missions. The project helps users discover historic spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments through searchable artifact cards, mission timelines, detailed explanations, and an interactive quiz. It addresses the challenge of making discarded space equipment and its scientific legacy easier to understand and explore. By bringing mission information and NASA image resources together in an accessible experience, SpaceStories turns forgotten hardware into engaging stories about exploration, engineering, and scientific discovery. The project aims to inspire students, educators, and space enthusiasts to learn more about planetary exploration and the lasting value of space missions.
details:
Project Overview

SpaceStories: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a responsive, browser-based educational application designed to make the stories of discarded space equipment easier to discover and understand. It focuses on selected artifacts from Apollo missions on the Moon and robotic missions on Mars.

How It Works

Users can:

  • Search artifacts by name, mission, or keyword.
  • Filter the collection by destination (Moon or Mars) and hardware type.
  • Open artifact cards to read what each object was designed to do, why it matters, and what happened to it.
  • Explore a timeline of important mission milestones.
  • Take a four-question interactive knowledge quiz.

The application uses JavaScript to organize and filter artifact information and retrieve relevant images from NASA's public Images and Video Library API when an internet connection is available. If an image cannot be retrieved, the application can still display the artifact information.

Benefits and Intended Impact

SpaceStories brings selected mission stories together in one accessible learning experience. It can help students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand planetary exploration, spacecraft engineering, scientific instruments, and the legacy of completed missions. Its goal is to turn the idea of equipment being “left behind” into an opportunity to learn about human exploration and scientific discovery.

Technology Used

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses the NASA Images and Video Library API to search for relevant NASA imagery. It is designed to run in a modern web browser and does not require a backend server or a user account.

Creativity and Design

The project combines searchable artifact discovery, plain-language storytelling, mission chronology, NASA imagery, and a knowledge quiz. Instead of presenting equipment as a simple list of objects, it connects each artifact to its purpose, mission, and scientific legacy.

Project Scope

This is an educational prototype. Its current collection focuses on selected Apollo, Mars Pathfinder, Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity mission artifacts. The collection can be expanded with additional missions, verified locations, and more NASA datasets in future versions.
